reasons: No test is visible in this file.
Data is fetched and state is updated inside the same request function, which is harder to reason about.
Loading, empty and error states are handled and shown clearly.

terms.meaning: A web address the app asks for data, such as the run events.
A rising number the server gives each event so the app can ask for only newer ones.
Asking the server again on a timer to get new data.
One box in the feed that groups everything known about one value.
Saved copy kept in the browser so the same item is not fetched again.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup
sections.what: Imports React tools, the data-fetching helper, icons and the request helper.

sections.name: FeedTool
sections.title: Feed tool names
sections.what: Names the three tools the feed supports: Reality Scan, Lessons Learnt and Opportunity Map.
sections.why: Limits the feed to these tools and documents its purpose.
sections.watch_out: A new tool name also needs matching events from the server.

sections.name: RunEvent, FeedResponse, Shot
sections.title: Event, reply and screenshot shapes
sections.what: Defines one recorded run event, the server's reply with events and counts, and the three screenshot states: ready, failed or queued.
sections.why: Sets the data the feed expects from the server.
sections.watch_out: Event payloads are loosely typed, so a missing field is ignored silently rather than reported.

sections.name: Card, Item
sections.title: Card and item shapes
sections.what: Defines a card with its sources, screenshot, alternative source, values, checks, decision and metric, and an item that is either a card or a short note.
sections.why: Gives the feed one structure to draw from.
sections.watch_out: Card fields fill in only as events arrive, so many are empty during a live run.

sections.name: fold
sections.title: Grouping events into cards
sections.what: Turns the raw event list into cards and notes. Events with the same card key are combined, later events fill or replace parts of the card, and events from before a stage restart are dropped.
sections.why: Likely reason: events arrive in small pieces, and the reader needs one card per value.
sections.watch_out: A stage restart removes that stage's earlier events, so cards from before the restart disappear.

sections.name: FILTERS, Filter
sections.title: Filter choices
sections.what: Lists the filter buttons: all, accepted, not used, couldn't capture and metrics.
sections.why: Lets a reader focus on one kind of card.
sections.watch_out: A new filter needs both a button here and a matching rule in the filter check.

sections.name: matches
sections.title: Filter check
sections.what: Decides whether one card passes the chosen filter. Held cards count as not used.
sections.why: Keeps the filter rules in one place.
sections.watch_out: Any filter outcome other than the three named decisions matches only by exact name.

sections.name: LiveRunFeed (part 1)
sections.title: Fetching events and building the view
sections.what: Fetches new events on a timer, keeps them in memory, combines them into cards, and works out the tally, the filter, the search and the follow setting.
sections.why: Likely reason: the feed must keep up with a run that is still writing events and update its counts without a page reload.
sections.watch_out: Polling stops when the run is no longer live and no screenshots are pending, so a late event may need a manual refresh; the file reads once more when the run stops to reduce this.

sections.name: LiveRunFeed (part 2)
sections.title: Feed layout
sections.what: Draws the header with the tally, filter buttons, search box and follow checkbox, then the card list with its show-more buttons and any empty or error message.
sections.why: Turns the current state into what the reader sees.
sections.watch_out: The show-more buttons only increase how many cards are displayed; they do not fetch older events.

sections.name: OUTCOME
sections.title: Decision badge styles
sections.what: Maps each decision (accepted, not used, held) to its label and colours.
sections.why: Keeps decision badges consistent across cards.
sections.watch_out: A decision not in this list falls back to the not used style.

sections.name: FeedCard (part 1)
sections.title: Value card
sections.what: Draws one value card: sources with an origin tag and link, screenshot, alternative source note, the value and unit, basis tags, quotes with their translation, check results, the decision note, and a warning when the screenshot reader found a passage the page reader missed.
sections.why: Gives the reader all the evidence for one value in one place.
sections.watch_out: The disagreement warning relies on the screenshot label containing the word verbatim, so a relabel would silently hide it.

sections.name: FeedCard (part 2)
sections.title: Value card ending
sections.what: This section holds no logic of its own; it is only the end of the value card layout.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: MetricCard
sections.title: Metric card
sections.what: Draws a computed metric with its label, a forecast or reported note, the formula and its inputs, or the reason it could not be computed.
sections.why: Shows how a number was calculated, so it can be checked.
sections.watch_out: The not-available case depends on one exact status word.

sections.name: ShotView
sections.title: Screenshot state
sections.what: Shows the screenshot area: a waiting box while queued, a note when capture failed, or the image otherwise, labelled as alternative source, stored or new.
sections.why: Lets the reader see the state of each screenshot.
sections.watch_out: Any state other than queued or failed is treated as ready.

sections.name: CaptureThumb
sections.title: Screenshot thumbnail
sections.what: Loads a screenshot from its address, shows a placeholder while it loads, an error message if it fails, and an image that toggles between a small and a full size on click.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the list compact while letting the reader enlarge an image.
sections.watch_out: Images are cached by address with no expiry, so a changed image at the same address will not refresh.

summary: A live list of what a running tool has read, showing sources, screenshots, values, checks and decisions as cards in the order they happened.
purpose: Lets a visitor watch or review a run's evidence as it arrives, with no text generated in the browser.
why: The header comment says every line is a stored run event, so the feed only shows recorded events.
how: Fetches run events from the run-events endpoint, asking only for events after the last sequence number seen, and repeats every 1.5 seconds while the run is live or screenshots are pending. Events are grouped into cards by card key, with later events filling in sources, screenshots, values, checks, decisions and metrics. A stage that ran again drops its earlier events. Filters, search and a follow option control what is shown, and a tally counts values, accepted items, screenshots and metrics.
inputs: The tool name, the run id, a live flag and optional stage labels. From the server: run events with sequence numbers, and counts of pending captures.
outputs: The rendered feed. Screenshots are loaded from stored addresses. Nothing is written back.
risks: The event list grows during long runs and is kept in memory, though only 40 cards are shown at a time. Screenshots are cached by address with no expiry.
debug: If the feed is empty, check the endpoint response for the run id and the live flag. If cards stay on Checking, look for a missing check result event. If counts are wrong, check the filter and the search box. If a screenshot fails, check its address and the capture events.
